metrics.justification: Handling of recurring rice supply and price shocks: announced relief measures including a BERNAS imported-white-rice gate-price cut (to RM2,800/tonne from 1 Dec 2024) and farmer flood aid, then a further cut (RM2,600/tonne, 15 May 2025) with RM150m to hold local white rice at RM2.60/kg. Measurable mitigation of a recurring crisis, not a structural resolution (anchor 2).

citation.title: Rice shortage due to floods to be addressed with imported rice price reduction, says Mat Sabu

metrics.justification: Incremental delivery: set a standardised Sabah/Sarawak padi floor price (RM1,300/tonne, effective 15 Feb 2024), but the marquee Control of Padi and Rice Act amendments to curb cartels were still pre-tabling as of 24 Feb 2026 and the BERNAS single-gatekeeper concession was retained. Partial reform with dilution (anchor 2).

citation.title: Laws to combat rice cartels to be tabled next Parliament meeting, says Mat Sabu

metrics.justification: Introduced a 'separation of powers' within the ministry splitting padi-industry development, rice regulation, and the BERNAS-representative roles to reduce conflict of interest. A documented structural move, but reported as administrative and not confirmed fully operative, so credited conservatively (anchor 2).

citation.title: MAFS Introduces Separation Of Powers, New Regulations To Bolster National Rice Production

metrics.justification: Candour under scrutiny: grilled by Opposition MPs on 19 Feb 2025 he admitted on the record that market manipulation was occurring and existing laws were inadequate, pledging a review; on 5 Feb 2026 he disclosed rice self-sufficiency was stagnant at ~52% against earlier higher ambitions. Acknowledged unflattering shortfalls with stated reasons (anchor 3).
